permitted_outcome: Operator staff act only under a sponsor DoA or a sponsor-approved JIT; the sponsor sees and approves operator access
prohibited_outcome: Operator workforce changes sponsor records outside the sponsor's exclusive legal control
governing_rules: Org §5.1 workforce role; CTL-031; DD-016; REG-001
finding_description: The authority model assumes workforce = sponsor staff. Under Models B/C the operator's staff are not covered by the sponsor's DoA, and the operator approves JIT itself. Requirement: operator access to tenant records needs a sponsor-side approver and a DoA link, and the sponsor receives the access log.

scenario: Enterprise payments pause triggered for a sponsor A incident halts sponsor B's year-end grants on the same platform
permitted_outcome: Kill switches scoped by tenant, partner, channel and agent; cross-tenant pause only for a platform-level incident, with notice
prohibited_outcome: Blast radius set by the switch design rather than by the incident
finding_description: CTL-028 defines only per-agent and enterprise pause. Scope (tenant/partner/channel), independence from a compromised control plane, and resume preconditions are unspecified. Payments-pause release is dual control (K §12) but nothing requires a review of changes made during the incident window.

scenario: Partner contracted with sponsors A and B requests a launch for a fund at A for a subject whose relationship exists only at B
permitted_outcome: Launch denied (ScopeDenied)
prohibited_outcome: Cross-sponsor launch

scenario: Launch artifact leaks through partner server access logs; attacker exchanges it before the user's browser does
permitted_outcome: Single use; the legitimate exchange gets ReplayRejected and raises a security event; short TTL; bound to origin and nonce
prohibited_outcome: Silent shared session

scenario: Attacker hijacks a donor session minutes after the donor completed passkey step-up for a $30k grant and, inside the 15-minute freshness window, submits $30k to a new recipient
permitted_outcome: Step-up for a new recipient or high value is bound to that transaction's canonical payload
prohibited_outcome: Time-window freshness authorizes an unrelated transaction
governing_rules: DD-021 action table (15 min freshness); TVCTL-06
finding_description: Sensitive-action assurance is time-window based (fresh within 15 min). Nothing binds the step-up or confirmation to the specific recipient and amount. Requirement: transaction-bound confirmation (sponsor-rendered payload hash in the WebAuthn challenge or RAR) for new recipients and above-threshold grants.

scenario: Captured SubmitGrantRecommendation replayed with the same idempotency key but a changed amount
permitted_outcome: Request-hash mismatch rejected; original receipt returned only for an identical request
prohibited_outcome: Second or altered recommendation

scenario: Old signed provider Returned webhook replayed to re-credit a fund a second time
permitted_outcome: Idempotent observation by provider event ID
prohibited_outcome: Double re-credit

scenario: Donor agent's DPoP key is software-held and is exfiltrated together with its token
permitted_outcome: Revocation; caps; new-recipient confirmation
prohibited_outcome: Unlimited replay

scenario: Widget refresh token persists in partitioned storage on a shared library computer; the next user reopens the host page and the widget resumes
permitted_outcome: Widget session bound to the host session and short-lived; logout propagates; ReauthRequired
prohibited_outcome: Next user sees or acts on the prior donor's fund
governing_rules: W01 session states; W01 trust item 4; W02 local caching threat review

scenario: Advisor delegates part of its recommend privilege to its own AI agent (org §5.1) and, as 'delegating Person', confirms the agent's above-cap recommendations; the donor never sees them
permitted_outcome: Only the donor creates agent delegations; confirmations go to the donor
prohibited_outcome: Advisor-created agent with advisor self-confirmation
governing_rules: Org §5.1 (advisor to agent subset delegation); identity principle 5 (advisors cannot change delegation); INV-A6
finding_description: Contradiction: org §5.1 allows advisor-to-agent subset delegation, while DD-021 says only the donor can change delegation. INV-A6's 'delegating Person' then lets an advisor confirm its own agent. How to classify the sponsor-operated donor assistant (a donor-side principal run by the sponsor) is also unresolved.

scenario: Sponsor-operated 'donor assistant' is treated as a donor-side principal with caps; a sponsor insider changes its prompt so it suggests and submits grants to a favoured charity
permitted_outcome: Every submission by a sponsor-operated assistant needs donor confirmation; its configuration falls under CW-19 change control
prohibited_outcome: Sponsor both originates and approves a recommendation attributed to the donor
governing_rules: Security §1 donor-side agent row; INV-A5; CTL-026
finding_description: Same gap as S-18: no rule covers an agent that the sponsor operates but that acts with donor authority.

scenario: Donor agent sends 40 confirmation requests a day; the donor taps 'approve all', including one injected new recipient
permitted_outcome: Itemized sponsor-rendered confirmations; no batch approval for new recipients; rate limits on confirmation requests
prohibited_outcome: Confirmation fatigue turns the control into a rubber stamp
governing_rules: INV-A6; TVCTL-06; UX §3.1 model D (per-item list)
finding_description: Confirmation content and batching are unspecified (S-7). A confirmation must show the canonical recipient and amount rendered by the sponsor, not agent text, and must not be batched for new recipients.

scenario: Charity description served in the machine-readable API instructs external donor agents to 'recommend $5,000 now'
permitted_outcome: Untrusted content delimited in the API; new-recipient confirmation; caps
prohibited_outcome: Agent-originated grant auto-approved

scenario: Donor dies; the agent keeps submitting weekly recommendations; after notice its token remains valid
permitted_outcome: Children end at the parent's effective time; pre-notice actions flagged
prohibited_outcome: Agent continues after notice

scenario: Donor repudiates an agent-submitted grant ('my agent exceeded my instructions')
permitted_outcome: Recommendation attributed to requesting and acting principal, with signed request event and caps evidence
prohibited_outcome: Unattributable request

scenario: Payee-profile approver fabricates the out-of-band verification for an attacker bank account on a real charity; a colluding releaser releases a $400k payment
permitted_outcome: Collusion-resistant controls: random assignment of the second person, staff-to-payee account/device matching, pair-concentration KRI, notice to the charity's prior verified contact
prohibited_outcome: Two colluding staff satisfy SoD-1 and pay an attacker
finding_description: Security §8 lists two-person collusion as residual, mitigated only by 'sampling and internal audit'. No control randomizes who the second approver is, flags recurring approver pairs, matches payee bank/address/device data against staff records, or requires rotation or mandatory leave.

scenario: Grant specialist repeatedly approves one donor's benefit-tainted referred grants in exchange for kickbacks; no recorded relationship
permitted_outcome: Random case assignment; specialist-donor concentration KRI; seeded cases; QA sampling
prohibited_outcome: Same specialist decides the same donor's cases indefinitely
finding_description: Same gap as S-1: case routing does not stop a reviewer from repeatedly receiving or picking one requester, and no KRI watches reviewer-requester concentration.

scenario: Policy author and publisher collude to loosen fuzzy-match sensitivity, labelling the change a tightening
permitted_outcome: Automated monotonic classification forces Change Board and CRCO; back-test shows the loosening
prohibited_outcome: Loosening published by two people

scenario: Payment releaser and the independent reconciler collude to clear the break for a misdirected payment
permitted_outcome: External auditor verification; write-off second approver; break aging escalation
prohibited_outcome: Break cleared and concealed
finding_description: TVCTL-07 makes reconciliation independent, but two-person collusion still defeats it (S-1). There is no pair KRI and no rotation requirement.

scenario: Engineer with JIT production write access edits a verified payee profile's bank token in the database while working a ticket
permitted_outcome: JIT scopes exclude payee, ledger and authority tables; any authoritative row change without a causing command is detected before payment
prohibited_outcome: Payment gate pays a hijacked but 'verified' profile
finding_description: CTL-031 says JIT exists, not what JIT may write. Direct data edits bypass CTL-004 and SM-1 because no command occurs. Requirement: no human write path to payee, authority, ledger or policy stores except domain commands; a continuous integrity check that every authoritative state change has a matching command event; and the payment gate refuses profiles whose state hash disagrees.

scenario: Break-glass account used at 03:00 to set a fund's AuthorityState and activate a successor; review is weekly
permitted_outcome: Break-glass cannot perform domain transitions; any use pages the CISO and holds affected subjects pending review
prohibited_outcome: Authority changed via break-glass and acted on before review
finding_description: Break-glass is 'sealed, alarmed and reviewed', but its permitted actions and a hold on affected subjects are not defined (S-9).

scenario: Data scientist relabels a real fraudulent referred grant as a CTL-046 seeded case so it is excluded from metrics and investigation
permitted_outcome: Seeded-case register held by internal audit, sealed and write-once; operators cannot label
prohibited_outcome: Real case hidden as a test
finding_description: Seeded cases (CTL-046) and canary grants (TVCTL-04) live in production, with no rule on who registers them, how they are kept out of financial and regulatory populations, or how a real item is protected from relabelling.

scenario: Engineer and a colluding code reviewer merge a payment-gate change that skips cooling-off for one payee flag
permitted_outcome: Change Board approval for control-touching deploys; production invariant tests on CTL-003
prohibited_outcome: Control bypass shipped by two developers

scenario: Grant approver pressures the sanctions officer to clear a true match on the same case
permitted_outcome: Sanctions officer clears only with evidence; approver is not the sanctions officer; flag never expires; escalation to GC
prohibited_outcome: Cleared to meet an SLA

scenario: Caller impersonating an elderly donor (P2) asks support to submit a $20k grant to a new charity by phone; staff enter it in the back office
permitted_outcome: Assisted-channel recommendation has a defined assurance (knowledge-based = AAL1), is attributed to staff plus donor, and a new recipient needs sponsor-direct confirmation
prohibited_outcome: Staff-entered request treated as donor-authenticated and auto-approved
finding_description: The UX requires a phone/human channel for P2/P4, but no requirement defines the assurance level of staff-entered (assisted) recommendations or profile changes, how they are attributed, or their limits. Social engineering of support becomes the cheapest account-takeover path.

scenario: Support agent uses 'view as donor' to troubleshoot and clicks Submit on the donor's draft
permitted_outcome: Support views are read-only; any donor-side command from staff is a distinct assisted command with evidence of the donor's instruction
prohibited_outcome: Command recorded as the donor's own
finding_description: Same gap as S-2: impersonation and view-as modes are not constrained.

scenario: Support JIT access to the identity vault for one case is used to download 500 ID images
permitted_outcome: JIT case-scoped and rate-limited; privileged-session detection in SIEM; review
prohibited_outcome: Bulk export unnoticed
governing_rules: CTL-031; AUTH-10; security §4 identity vault; security §5 SIEM

scenario: SIM-swapped attacker passes help-desk recovery; the prior-channel notice goes to the hijacked phone
permitted_outcome: Cooling-off before payout-relevant actions; notice to all prior channels including email
prohibited_outcome: Immediate grant rights after recovery

scenario: AG-04 dossier cites 'IRS determination letter p.2 confirms public charity status' but the snapshot says private foundation; the specialist relies on the citation
permitted_outcome: Citations mechanically verified against the cited snapshot before display; unverified claims marked
prohibited_outcome: Hallucinated citation drives an approval
finding_description: Grounding checks (CTL-039) apply only to the donor-facing service agent. Staff- and board-facing outputs (AG-03, AG-04, AG-07, AG-18, AG-19) have no citation-fidelity check, yet they feed human decisions.

scenario: AG-19 board narrator misstates the fallback rate and exception backlog in the board pack used to renew the routine-approval delegation
permitted_outcome: Figures in board drafts tied to approved snapshot fields and verified
prohibited_outcome: Board renews the delegation on invented figures
finding_description: Same gap as S-11.

scenario: Model provider silently updates the model behind the same alias; AG-02, AG-03 and AG-17 false negatives rise together and the falling flag rate is masked by the December surge
permitted_outcome: Pinned immutable model snapshots; provider change detected; continuous known-answer canaries per agent
prohibited_outcome: Correlated silent loss of protective flags
finding_description: A model change counts as a version change (security §9.3), but nothing pins immutable snapshots or detects a provider-side change under the same name. Agents sharing one model fail together, and flag-rate drift detection can be hidden by volume. Requirement: pinning, continuous canary sets and a correlation analysis across agents.

scenario: AG-04 summary and AG-02 flag come from the same base model; the reviewer treats their agreement as independent corroboration
permitted_outcome: Shared-model provenance shown; same-model outputs not counted as independent evidence
prohibited_outcome: Correlated AI outputs presented as two lines of defence
finding_description: Same gap as S-10: there is no independence rule for AI outputs that share a model.

scenario: Insider edits the AG-02 system prompt and retrieval exclusions in a config repository; this is not treated as a model or permission change
permitted_outcome: Prompts, retrieval sources and thresholds are versioned agent configuration under CTL-026 and SoD-8
prohibited_outcome: Silent behaviour change suppresses benefit flags
finding_description: CTL-026 gates versions and permission expansions; security §9.3 names model and provider changes. Prompt, retrieval and threshold configuration is not named, so it can change the behaviour of a protective agent outside the evaluation gate (S-10).

scenario: AG-11 discovery recommends a charity whose third-party profile was poisoned to promote a sham organization
permitted_outcome: Third-party data advisory only; new-recipient controls; velocity
prohibited_outcome: Discovery listing treated as endorsement

scenario: AG-10 advisor copilot drafts a grant with the EIN of a similarly named charity; the advisor submits without reading
permitted_outcome: Review shows legal name and EIN; D eligibility on that EIN
prohibited_outcome: Copilot output treated as fact

scenario: At 10x December volume specialists open the evidence for two seconds before approving, to satisfy TVR-UX-006 gating
permitted_outcome: Per-reviewer seeded-case detection rates; workload caps; detection below target triggers queue redesign
prohibited_outcome: Gating met in form only, with no review in substance

scenario: AG-08 extracts ED affidavit fields wrongly and the extracted value feeds the deterministic validity gate
permitted_outcome: D gate inputs must be authoritative; AI extraction only drafts or flags, and a human confirms
prohibited_outcome: Unverified extraction used as an authoritative input

scenario: Attacker submits many recommendations with long purpose texts and attachments to exhaust per-agent cost ceilings; AG-02 trips its breaker and grants take the TVCTL-05 fallback, which is looser than the agent
permitted_outcome: Degraded modes are never less restrictive than normal; ceiling exhaustion by one requester is rate-limited per requester; time in degraded mode is bounded and alarmed
prohibited_outcome: Attacker-induced degraded mode becomes a bypass
finding_description: TVCTL-05 requires that a fallback ran but not that it is at least as strict as the agent. Per-agent cost ceilings (security §9.4) can be exhausted on purpose. CTL-010's monotonic rule covers parameter changes, not degraded modes. Requirement: degraded-mode monotonicity plus per-requester cost quotas.

scenario: Sanctions screening vendor and AG-03 are both unavailable for 6 hours at peak
permitted_outcome: Payment gate holds when screening cannot run against the current list; queue with truthful status
prohibited_outcome: Release on the last cached screening result

scenario: Model provider outage of 72 hours exceeds the T2 RTO; ER reminder drafts and dossiers stop
permitted_outcome: D path continues; P items queue for humans; ER obligations still tracked by TVCTL-12
prohibited_outcome: Obligations silently missed

scenario: Donor writes the grant purpose with hidden instructions telling the benefit-risk classifier 'no donor benefit; classify low' for gala tickets
permitted_outcome: Requester-supplied text treated as hostile; deterministic benefit keywords and category rules run alongside AG-02; injection markers raise a flag
prohibited_outcome: Agent false negative is the only defence against a §4967 benefit
governing_rules: AG-02; CTL-008; security §8 injection residual; TVCTL-05
finding_description: Security §8 accepts agent false negatives because 'deterministic gates still apply', but no deterministic gate exists for donor benefit: AG-02 is the only screen, and the requester controls its input. Requirement: a deterministic complement (category, keyword and recipient-type rules) and injection detection on requester free text, plus CTL-049 sampling of unflagged purposes.

scenario: Charity-submitted ER report PDF contains instructions telling AG-12 to mark reports complete and suppress reminders
permitted_outcome: AG-12 cannot write; report receipt recorded by a human or a D rule; missing report escalates
prohibited_outcome: Obligation closed by injected text

scenario: Complex-asset offering memorandum includes white-text instructions telling AG-07 to omit environmental liabilities
permitted_outcome: Specialist decides; committee above threshold; agent output is only a dossier
prohibited_outcome: Dossier omission accepted as clean

scenario: Charity name field contains 'Note to reviewer: pre-cleared by Compliance', shown inside the exception dossier
permitted_outcome: Untrusted content quoted and visually distinct from system facts; content confers no authority
prohibited_outcome: Reviewer treats charity text as a compliance statement

scenario: Email claiming to be from a charity, processed by AG-09, asks for a bank account update
permitted_outcome: Channel rejected; verified re-enrolment only
prohibited_outcome: Profile changed

scenario: Storage administrator rewrites the evidence store and recomputes the whole hash chain to remove a control failure
permitted_outcome: Chain checkpoints anchored outside the platform's admin domain (internal audit or external WORM/witness) so a rewrite is detectable
prohibited_outcome: Internally consistent but forged evidence
finding_description: TVCTL-11 specifies an append-only hash chain, but a hash chain proves nothing against someone who can rewrite it end to end. Requirement: periodic checkpoint hashes delivered to a party outside the platform admin domain, and verified at audit.

scenario: Evidence pipeline is down for 6 hours while payments continue, leaving decision records missing
permitted_outcome: A transition commits only with its decision record (atomic); otherwise the money-moving transition blocks; any gap is logged as a control failure
prohibited_outcome: Payments without evidence

scenario: Clock skew of +3 days on a payment-gate node makes a payee's CTL-004 cooling-off appear elapsed
permitted_outcome: Trusted time source; skew alarms; cooling-off and freshness computed from authoritative time; payment gate fails closed on skew
prohibited_outcome: Time-based controls defeated by a wrong clock
finding_description: Many controls are time-based (cooling-off, 15-minute freshness, effective-time authority, return windows, data freshness SLOs), but no requirement names an authoritative time source, a skew tolerance or fail-closed behaviour.

scenario: TVCTL-04 canary grants and CTL-046 seeded cases appear in the auditor's sample population and in 990 Schedule D grant counts
permitted_outcome: Seeded items registered, excluded from financial and regulatory populations by a controlled join, and never move real money
prohibited_outcome: Regulatory filings or audit samples contaminated by test items
finding_description: Same gap as S-15: there is no population-exclusion rule for seeded items.

scenario: Point-in-time restore: T1 grant decisioning (RPO 15 min) and T0 payment gate (RPO 5 min) restore to different points, leaving PaymentInstructed without GrantApproved
permitted_outcome: Consistent cross-tier restore point, or decision records in the same tier as payments; post-restore invariant check before resuming
prohibited_outcome: INV-A3 violated after restore; payments with no approval record
finding_description: DR tiers put the payment gate (T0) and grant decisioning (T1) at different RPOs and assign no tier to the evidence store. A restore can break INV-A3 and TVCTL-11. Requirement: one restore-consistency group for decision, payment and evidence records, and an invariant suite that must pass before payments resume.

scenario: Payment gate restored to 5 minutes earlier loses two attempts the provider already Accepted; the grants look Funded with no attempt; ops create new attempts
permitted_outcome: Attempt creation durable with RPO 0 before submission, or mandatory provider reconciliation of the RPO window before any new attempt
prohibited_outcome: Double payment after restore
governing_rules: PA-1; PA-3; TVCTL-02; security §7 RPO 5 min
finding_description: PA-1 assumes local attempt state is complete. With a 5-minute RPO, attempts can vanish locally while live at the provider. TVS-076 covered failover with durable state, not a lossy restore. Requirement: RPO 0 for attempt records, or a blocking provider-side reconciliation of the RPO window.

scenario: Ransomware encrypts the primary systems and online backups
permitted_outcome: Immutable or offline backups; cold-standby restore tested; payments paused until invariants are verified
prohibited_outcome: Restore from a tampered backup; unknown payment state

scenario: Workforce identity platform compromised; the kill-switch console uses the same SSO and attackers lock responders out
permitted_outcome: Kill switch operable through an out-of-band path independent of the compromised IdP, with sealed credentials and two-person activation
prohibited_outcome: Responders unable to pause payments during an active attack
finding_description: Same gap as S-16: the kill switch's independence from the compromised plane is not required.

scenario: After a 2-day payments pause for a payee-hijack incident, dual control releases the pause; queued payments include profiles, delegations and recovery factors changed during the incident window
permitted_outcome: Resume requires a review and re-verification of every payee, delegation and recovery change made in the window
prohibited_outcome: Bulk release of payments to profiles altered by the attacker
governing_rules: CTL-028; K §12 pause release dual control; SM-6; CTL-004
finding_description: Same gap as S-16: SM-6 re-checks status at release but does not re-verify profiles marked verified during the compromise.

scenario: Defective AG-17 version raises 20,000 false related-party flags in December; INV-A4 blocks approvals; staff propose a database bulk clear
permitted_outcome: Governed class-level supersession: a named person decides for the defective version's flags, with sampling and a record; no direct data edit
prohibited_outcome: Ad hoc bulk clear, or year-end stall
finding_description: Class-level (bulk) decisions are unspecified. Flags from a quarantined agent version need a governed supersession path, or staff will improvise (S-19).

scenario: Provider degradation at 10x volume leaves 4,000 Unknown attempts; ops propose a bulk 'NotReceived' to meet year-end
permitted_outcome: Unknown resolves per attempt on provider evidence, or through a provider-attested batch reconciliation file; bulk human resolution prohibited
prohibited_outcome: Mass duplicate payments
finding_description: PA-2 and TVCTL-02 define one decision with two approvers, but nothing prohibits a class-level PA-2 decision under volume pressure, and there is no provider-side batch-proof path. Requirement: bulk Unknown resolution only on provider-attested evidence per attempt.

scenario: Partner compromise discovered; the sponsor must list every recommendation made through that partner's integration during the window
permitted_outcome: Token-exchange actor and partner client recorded on each command; query by partner and time
prohibited_outcome: Cannot scope the incident

scenario: 10x December surge trips enterprise-window fan-out caps for legitimate grants; ops raise the caps under pressure
permitted_outcome: Raising caps is a loosening (Change Board plus CRCO); seasonal parameters pre-approved with expiry
prohibited_outcome: Caps raised informally mid-surge

scenario: A sanctions list update during a 10x surge needs a full rescreen; payments are submitted before the rescreen finishes on the new list
permitted_outcome: Payment gate re-checks against the current list version at submission; data-freshness block
prohibited_outcome: Release screened only against the superseded list

scenario: Screen-reader user approves a CIBA/push confirmation whose OS notification truncates the recipient and amount
permitted_outcome: Confirmation content fully perceivable through AT (sponsor page, not truncated OS text); accessible alternative before approval
prohibited_outcome: User confirms a transaction they could not perceive
finding_description: UXA-3 covers an accessible authentication method, not accessible presentation of what is being confirmed. Out-of-band confirmations and regenerated previews have no requirement that the transaction details are perceivable, and that changes are announced, before consent.

scenario: Preview expires during a slow assistive-technology review; the regenerated preview changes a percentage-derived amount from $9,800 to $9,200 without announcement; the user submits
permitted_outcome: Material change between previews highlighted and announced; renewed explicit review
prohibited_outcome: Submission on a superseded mental model
finding_description: Same gap as S-17: UXA-4 restores the draft but does not require that preview changes be announced.

scenario: User with a comma-decimal locale types '1.000' meaning one thousand and it is parsed as $1.00; another types '5,000' meaning five and gets $5,000
permitted_outcome: Locale-explicit parsing; review states the amount in currency and words; large-change warning
prohibited_outcome: Silent mis-scaled amount

scenario: Charity combobox selects on arrow focus; a screen-reader user tabs away leaving an adjacent similarly named charity selected
permitted_outcome: Explicit activation; review reads legal name, city and EIN in order
prohibited_outcome: Wrong recipient chosen silently

scenario: State AG subpoena requires partner-side launch and event logs; the partner was offboarded and has already given a deletion attestation (WG-7)
permitted_outcome: Deletion obligations subordinate to legal-hold notices; partner contract includes preservation on notice
prohibited_outcome: Evidence destroyed under a sponsor-mandated deletion
finding_description: WG-7 requires partners to delete received data on exit, with no carve-out for legal holds or regulatory inquiries.

scenario: SOC 1 auditor requests the population of routine D approvals in a period, each with its linked board delegation
permitted_outcome: Per-decision policy-version and delegation link; population with numerator, denominator and status
prohibited_outcome: Population drawn from a projection without provenance

scenario: IRS examiner asks why a D-path grant was approved two years ago
permitted_outcome: Decision record with policy version, input snapshot hash and eligibility data version
prohibited_outcome: Reconstruction from current data

scenario: External auditor's read-only account (P15) is phished and used to export full populations
permitted_outcome: Scoped, time-bound auditor access with phishing-resistant MFA; no identity-vault access; export volume alerts
prohibited_outcome: Auditor account becomes a bulk exfiltration path

scenario: In a dispute, a regulator asks what the donor was shown (available estimate and disclaimers) when submitting
permitted_outcome: GrantPreview content and hash retained with the submission
prohibited_outcome: Cannot prove what was displayed
